item.title: Still Here Fest - Beloved Asheville Benefit — Fri Sep 18, 7:00 PM — NC
item.description:
Still Here Fest is a celebration of the resilience of the Western North Carolina community. After the horrific events of Hurricane Helene, cities like Asheville and many others in the region saw firsthand the power and the strength of love and empathy. Spearheading the relief efforts, groups like Beloved Asheville and so many others dropped everything to serve, care for, and feed their community, neighbors, friends, and strangers alike. At the front of many of these relief efforts were the artists and musicians, putting aside their creative drive to take time to bring food, water, and other life-saving supplies to those in need. Still Here Fest 2026 is in recognition of not only the efforts of these groups and individuals but also the resilient spirit of Western North Carolina. We survive, we thrive, we are still here.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

Rising AppalachiaIn Appalachia, farmers still practice the ancestral tradition of companion planting. Corn grows tall as a trellis, beans climb the corn, and squash provides the ground cover. Rising Appalachia cultivates a similar symbiosis in their music, where Southern folk traditions, New Orleans swamp culture, and Atlanta’s street spirit strengthen each other. Known for their seamless harmonies, songcatching and storytelling, the band has released ten albums and toured throughout North America, South America, Europe, the Celtic Isles, Australia and beyond — performing everywhere from the Telluride Bluegrass Festival and Red Rocks to NPR’s Tiny Desk. After spearheading the alt-country movement with Uncle Tupelo, Jay Farrar pursued his vision with Son Volt, who recorded three landmark albums in the ’90s before the groundbreaking artist put the band on extended hiatus and cut three solo LPs. Missing the free exchange of ideas and the surprises that inevitably occur when a group of simpatico musicians lock together, Farrar assembled a new lineup of Son Volt in 2004 and has since released nine albums. The latest album, Sound Signal Serenades, was released as a special 2026 Record Store Day limited edition LP. Jay Farrar’s work often seeks out the ghosts of America’s discordant or forgotten past, converses at length with them, and writes songs that stake a claim to a better future.

item.title: The Southern Highland Craft Guild's 46th Annual Heritage Weekend — Sat Sep 19, 10:00 AM — Folk Art Center
item.description:
You are invited to our 46th. annual Heritage Weekend on September 19 and 20 at the Folk Art Center on the Blue Ridge Parkway. Many of you have been to this fun event in the past and we will again host over 20 heritage artist, musicians and dancers to honor and celebrate Mountain Heritage Crafts. One of the highlights of the celebration is our Annual World Gee Haw Whimmy Diddle competition on Saturday afternoon. A Whimmy Diddle is an Appalachian mountain toy, traditionally made from 2 sticks of rhododendron. Notches are carved into the stick and a propeller is attached to the end. Rubbing the notches with the second stick makes the propeller spin! The trick is to make it spin gee (to the right) or haw (to the left). Contestants are judged by their skills and interesting prizes will be awarded. The music stage will provide entertainment with Blue Grass and Gospel music, and cloggers will demonstrate the mountain dance tradition.

item.title: Sam Knob; a Saunter — Thu Sep 24, 9:15 AM
item.description: Hendo Fun Friends Darlene will lead to Sam Knob in the Black Balsam area of the BRPwy; Up to 12 of you are welcome. After a ½ mile walk through the meadow. the climb is just shy of 400 ft. in ½ mile via several switchbacks on the trail. We pass a lush, young forest of mostly northern hardwood trees. There are many roots and rocky areas along the trail. Lush vegetation grows near rock outcrops beside the trail, including blueberries, strawberries, sedges and grass, mountain laurel, Carolina rhododendron, and countless wildflowers including bluets. The trail will pass beneath some large rock outcrops, which lie just below the summit. We’ll reach a grassy, shrubby saddle between the two high knobs, and a large outcropping of snow white quartz rocks from a grassy meadow. Difficulty: Trail Tread Condition: Moderately Rough; Constant moderate climb. Rocky. item.title: Lea and Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp — Fri Oct 9, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Gaelynn Lea and Kalyn Rose Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp will visit UNC Asheville for an afternoon talk and evening performance. At 3 p.m., Lea and Heffernan will discuss disability culture, access, and activism, sharing their experiences as artists and advocates working to make the arts more inclusive. At 6 p.m., Wheelchair Sports Camp will take the stage for a free performance. Lea, winner of NPR Music’s Tiny Desk Contest, is an accomplished violinist, songwriter, composer, and disability advocate who has performed around the world and composed the score for Macbeth on Broadway. Wheelchair Sports Camp, led by wheelchair-using rapper Kalyn Rose Heffernan, blends hip-hop, humor, and high-energy performance. The Denver-based band has expanded its work beyond music into performance art, museums, theater, film, and activism. Both events are free and open to the public and will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of the Highsmith Student Union.

item.title: Guided Trail Walk — Sat Oct 10, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

item.title: The Haunted Farm — Sat Oct 10, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Asheville 20s-40s Social Group The Haunted Farm is Western North Carolina’s Scariest Attraction, and has been Voted Best Haunted House in NC!
Located in rural farmland near Hendersonville, The Haunted Farm sits on a mysterious, blood-soaked stretch of land where the locals claim an age-old Blood Feud between the Lively and Tate families has devastated the local farming community. The dark Haunted History of Curses, Derangements, Undead, Ghosts, and terrible Bloodshed brings visitors from near and far – hoping to survive The Haunted Farm.
It is advised you buy a ticket in advance incase they sell out but it is not mandatory according to the website! It is not recommended if you have any serious heart or anxiety conditions, or are pregnant. They have a “chicken run” for those who need a safe word and underwear for sale if you pee your pants.
Get your tickets at: https://nchauntedfarm.fearticket.com/
Source: Asheville 20s-40s Social Group
